questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Would you repair the bike?

options.text: Would have the bike repaired by you?
Would the bike repaired by you?
Would you be repaired by the bike?
Would the bike be repaired by you?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The structure of the passive voice sentence should be: ***auxiliary verb + past participle + by + agent*.**
 
• The correct transformation of **"Would you repair the bike?" **in passive voice is** "Would the bike be repaired by you?".**
 
• Options 1, 2, and 3 do not follow the correct structure for passive voice.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"Would the bike be repaired by you?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Would have the bike repaired by you?"** – Incorrect structure and tense.
 
• **Option 2: "Would the bike repaired by you?"** – Missing auxiliary verb "be".
 
• **Option 3: "Would you be repaired by the bike?"** – Incorrect subject and object placement.

questions.question:
Select the correct option to form a meaningful sentence.

I can't (a)/ to (b)/ see (c)/ of (d)/ dogs (e)/ rehomed (f)/ bear (g)/ pictures (h)/ rescued (i)/ waiting (j)/ to be (k)

options.text: a, k, b, h, d, i, j, g, f, c, e
a, j, b, c, d, i, e, k, g, f, h
a, b, h, i, e, j, k, f, g, c, d
a, g, b, c, h, d, i, e, j, k, f

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To form a meaningful sentence, the words need to be in the correct order to convey a logical and coherent message.
 
• The correct sequence is:** "I can't bear to see pictures of rescued dogs waiting to be rehomed."**
 
• Breaking it down: 
 
 
• a) I can't
 
• g) bear
 
• b) to
 
• c) see
 
• h) pictures
 
• d) of
 
• i) rescued
 
• e) dogs
 
• j) waiting
 
• k) to be
 
• f) rehomed
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: a, k, b, h, d, i, j, g, f, c, e - This sequence does not form a logical sentence order.
 
• Option 2: a, j, b, c, d, i, e, k, g, f, h - This sequence does not form a logical sentence order.
 
• **Option 3**: a, b, h, i, e, j, k, f, g, c, d - This sequence does not form a logical sentence order.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

The teacher praised the students for their excellent performance.

options.text: The students are praised by the teacher for their excellent performance.
The students were praised by the teacher for their excellent performance.
The students had been praised by the teacher for their excellent performance.
The students were being praised by the teacher for their excellent performance.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is originally in active voice: **"The teacher praised the students for their excellent performance."**
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the** passive sentence.**
 
• The verb **"praised"** is in the past tense, so in passive voice, it should be **"were praised."**
 
• The correct structure for the passive sentence is: **"The students were praised by the teacher for their excellent performance."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The students are praised by the teacher for their excellent performance." - This is incorrect because the verb "are praised" is in the present tense.
 
• **Option 3:** "The students had been praised by the teacher for their excellent performance." - This is incorrect because the verb "had been praised" is in the past perfect tense.
 
• **Option 4:** "The students were being praised by the teacher for their excellent performance." - This is incorrect because the verb "were being praised" is in the past continuous tense.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Close the curtains!
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence **"Close the curtains!" is an imperative sentence (a command).**
 
• When changing an imperative sentence into the passive voice, the structure** "Let + object + be + past participle**" is used.
 
• Thus, **"Close the curtains!" becomes "Let the curtains be closed!" **in **passive voice.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2**: Let the curtains fall close! - This option is not correct as it changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3**: Let the curtains be close! - This option is incorrect as it grammatically incorrect and does not convey the intended command.
 
• **Option 4**: Let the curtains become closed! - This option is also incorrect as it is not the correct passive form for an imperative sentence.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• The sentence requires the **simple past tense to indicate a completed action in the past.**
 
• **"Had" **is the **correct form of the past tense** for the verb** "have" **in this context.
 
• Options 1, 3, and 4 are incorrect as they do not use the simple past tense appropriately.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"I** had** a headache earlier, but I feel fine now."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3: "have"** - This is the present tense and does not fit the context of a completed action in the past.
 
• **Option 4: "am having"** - This is the present continuous tense, which is not suitable for describing a past event.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The principal said, “A biometric device will be installed from the next week.”

options.text: The principal said that a biometric device would be installed the for following week.
The principal said that a biometric device will be installed the next week.
The principal said that a biometric device would be installed from the following week.
The principal said that a biometric device would have been installed the following week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting direct speech to indirect speech, the tense of the verb often changes. In this case,** "will be installed" becomes "would be installed."**
 
• The phrase** "from the next week"** changes to **"from the following week"** to maintain the correct sequence of time in reported speech.
 
• The correct transformation of the sentence is: **"The principal said that a biometric device would be installed from the following week."**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"The principal said that a biometric device would be installed from the following week."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The principal said that a biometric device would be installed the for following week." - This option is incorrect because of the incorrect usage of "the for following week."
 
• **Option 2:** "The principal said that a biometric device will be installed the next week." - This option is incorrect because "will be installed" should change to "would be installed" in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 4:** "The principal said that a biometric device would have been installed the following week." - This option is incorrect because "would have been installed" implies a condition that was not fulfilled.
